summary: Second documenting pass over M1-S02 (ui, scale project, design-only), after three org-driven layout repairs that landed between the first pass (2026-09-15T20-18-25Z) and this one. Precondition held: the step was tested, tests/M1-S02/results.json carries "passed": true with fresh artefact_hashes, and its newest envelope is the step-tester's 2026-09-18T14-00-27Z run. PLAN.md and CLARIFICATIONS.md were re-rendered from plan.json (exit 0). Two entries were appended to decisions.md: D-M1S02-07, a deviation recording all three repairs (N3-F-02 added Probability as Required; N3-F-03 set Name Required; N3-F-04 set StageName Required with CloseDate set in the same pass), what they supersede in D-M1S02-01/D-M1S02-02, and the library filing; and O-M1S02-04, the residue run 4 did not settle. Four workbook rows were replaced in place, keyed by row_id (CWB-LAYOUT-001/002 in Section 2 - Page Layouts + Lightning Pages, the section the ui step type maps to; CWB-OTHER-003/004 in the Other configuration default section, where Step 4 routes a package.xml and a deploy-order note that are not migration artefacts), and three traceability rows (REQ-008, REQ-009, REQ-010). The rows now state the four Required items, the checker's current findings (1 REVIEW + 1 INFO, replacing the two 'marks no field behavior=Required' INFOs the 2026-09-15 rows carried), and the org evidence: reports/MOCK-DEPLOY-M1.md run 4, Succeeded, 9/9 components. One claim was deliberately NOT carried forward as confirmed: run 4 proves the shipped four-item set validates, not that CloseDate is itself platform-required - it was never named by the org - so the UNVERIFIED (2026-09-18) marker in artefacts/M1-S02/deploy-order.md section 6 still stands, contradicting run 4's note that it 'resolves to confirmed at the next doc-keeper pass'; this agent also does not write inside artefacts/. The tester's drift finding is recorded as O-M1S02-04 with the exact amend-step --prose-only command for the planner; plan.json prose was not touched. Checkers run and reported honestly: check_workbook.py exit 1 on both slices (9 and 10 issues, every one a 'Missing canonical section' for a section a per-step slice does not carry, zero row-level findings - confirmed meaningful by a positive control that made the linter reject a planted placeholder status), and check_rtm.py exit 1 (10 rows, 0 orphans, 1 error, 14 warnings). That one error is new to the file and true: normalising REQ-010's status cell from '**In Build**' to the bare enum token surfaced a coverage gap the bold markers had been hiding as a waived WARN - REQ-010 has no test because no declared test reads for a relatedLists element. It is reported, not papered over. M1-S02 moved tested -> documented (set-status exit 0, 23 plan-wide checker-coverage WARNs printed, 2 of them this step's). Milestone M1's gate is pending and has never been approved, so the next action is M1's FIRST verification, not a section 8 re-verification.
confidence_rationale: Step 11 table, MEDIUM row: two of the step's four artefacts (package.xml, deploy-order.md) are placed in the Other configuration default section rather than a numbered one - the judgment Step 4's docs row asks for (are they migration artefacts? no), so a placed row with a flag rather than a dropped one. Not HIGH for two further reasons this run turned up: an ERROR now stands in traceability.md (REQ-010 has no test id while status is In Build), and a claim the sources disagree about - whether CloseDate is platform-required - was resolved by writing the weaker true statement rather than the stronger one the mock-deploy report invited. Every row does carry a real source_req_id and a verification cell, and re-running produced no duplicates.

dimensions_skipped.reason: check_workbook.py recognises a section only from a heading matching '^#{2,3}\s+Section\s+(\d+)\s*[---]\s*(.+)$', so the rows under the 'Other configuration' heading in workbook/99-other-configuration.md (CWB-OTHER-003, CWB-OTHER-004) were parsed into no section and were not row-validated - only the Section 2 rows were. The file's own intro already documents this gap; numbering it 'Section 11' would invent an eleventh canonical section, which admin/configuration-workbook-authoring Concept 2 forbids.
dimensions_skipped.retry_hint: Re-lint those two rows on the M4-S03 compile run, where they land under a recognised canonical heading, or extend check_workbook.py to parse an 'Other configuration' heading.

process_observations.observation: The three repairs are fully reconstructable from the build's own record without reading the artefacts: each org message is quoted verbatim in reports/MOCK-DEPLOY-M1.md, each fix has its own metadata-builder envelope with a decision_record entry naming the gotcha it rests on, and deploy-order.md section 6 carries a write-up per round. That is what let this pass write D-M1S02-07 from sources rather than from inference.

The library has already been through this exact failure once, on Case: examples/builds/case-onboarding/decisions.md D-M1S02-05 records four layout-required Case facts found the same way, and the remedy that closed it was checker rules RL-REQ-01/02 in admin/record-types-and-page-layouts plus gotchas 12 and 13. Those two gotchas are exactly what let this build's builder read run 1's message correctly on the first try and write Required rather than Edit - the earlier deepening paid off in a different object's build.

The checker's layout-required rules are still Case-only by construction - CASE_LAYOUT_REQUIRED_ITEMS is a three-name tuple with the comment 'do not extend this to another object without a dry run', and RL-REQ-03 is an ADVISORY name-like-field smoke test for every other standard object. So the four Opportunity facts this build bought with four mock-deploy rounds are not yet encoded anywhere a checker can enforce them, and the next Opportunity build in this library will rediscover them the same way unless Cursor task 18 lands. The step's declared checker passed clean both before and after the repairs, which is correct behaviour for a rule set that does not cover Opportunity - and is also why no gate in this loop caught it.

reports/MOCK-DEPLOY-M1.md run 4 instructs that the UNVERIFIED (2026-09-18) marker on CloseDate 'resolves to confirmed at the next doc-keeper pass'. This pass did not resolve it, on two independent grounds, and both are worth a human's attention: the doc keeper does not write inside artefacts/ (so the instruction named an agent that cannot carry it out), and run 4's evidence proves the four-item set is sufficient to validate, not that CloseDate is individually necessary - it was set one round ahead of any finding and no org message ever named it. Recorded as O-M1S02-04 with a one-round close condition rather than rounded up.

evidence.path: reports/MOCK-DEPLOY-M1.md run 4; artefacts/M1-S02/deploy-order.md section 6 'Third discovery (run 3)'; agents/build-doc-keeper/AGENT.md 'What This Agent Does NOT Do'

process_observations.observation: Normalising REQ-010's status cell from '**In Build**' to the bare enum token 'In Build' turned a waived WARN into an ERROR in check_rtm.py: the bold markers had put the value outside the closed status enum, and the linter waives a coverage gap on a status it does not recognise as a build status. Emphasis markup inside an enum cell is therefore not cosmetic - it silently suppresses the rule that cell drives. The gap it was hiding is real (REQ-010 has no artefact and no test, which the row has said in prose since 2026-09-15), so the error is left standing and named rather than re-hidden.

build_plan.py set-status printed 23 section-5 checker-coverage WARNs plan-wide this run, two of them M1-S02's own (admin/opportunity-management ships check_opportunity_management.py and admin/products-and-pricebooks ships check_products_and_pricebooks.py, neither declared as an acceptance test on the step or on milestone M1). Unchanged from the tester's run and not a defect in the artefacts, but the M1 gate is where a human sees the count, and amend-step --add-checker is the one-line remedy for the two on this step.

evidence.path: build_plan.py set-status plan.json M1-S02 documented, stderr this run

process_observations.observation: check_rtm.py's 14 warnings are mostly a standing disagreement between this build's writing conventions and the linter's expectations, not defects: every source cell in this matrix is multi-valued ('Q20, Q14, Q22, D2') and every decision_ref uses the doc keeper's own D-M<m>S<nn>-<nn> ids rather than the plan's bare D<n>, both of which the linter flags. Changing either would lose information, so nothing was changed; whether the linter or the convention should move is a call for whoever owns the RTM skill, not for a documentation pass.

The two layouts remain byte-identical after all three repairs - both files were repaired identically and their artefact_hashes are the same digest - so the merge question O-M1S02-03 raised on 2026-09-15 is exactly as open as it was, and the repairs are evidence on its side rather than against it: the platform's required set is a property of the object, not of the record type, so nothing the org said differentiates the pair. Still a human's call at the M1 gate; this pass asserts no answer.

Both M1 steps are now documented and gate milestone:M1 is pending with no by/at - this is M1's FIRST verification, not a section 8 re-verification of an accepted milestone. build_plan.py next confirms it: "gate 'milestone:M1' is 'pending', not 'approved'". The M1-S01 doc-keeper envelope of 2026-09-18T13-56-11Z reached the same reading independently, so no envelope in this build contradicts it.
